messages.content: Predict an actual human monetary decision in an anonymous computer business simulation. Three co-owners form one fixed company/group. They cannot communicate or see one another across partitions. Each round has one sales leader with a fresh salary of L$80 and two team members with L$50 each. Rank and therefore salary can change between rounds. L$ denotes laboratory dollars. Unspent earlier earnings cannot be added to the new salary. The final number of rounds has not been announced to participants. Each person receives CAN$5 for attending,plus the average payable L$earnings per round converted at L$3=CAN$1. Practice does not enter paid earnings. Each round has TWO successive choices. First,everyone simultaneously chooses an integer signed manipulation m from−10through10. A positive m spends m laboratory dollars to increase the threat announcement by5percentage points per dollar;negative m spends|m|to decrease it by5percentage points per dollar;0spends nothing. Spending costs|m|,regardless of direction. The current true failure chance and current announcement are unknown at this first choice. Manipulation changes only the announcement,never the true chance. All members’ changes are added to the underlying threat,and the resulting announcement is bounded to0–100%. This announcement is then shown to everyone. Second,each simultaneously contributes a whole-dollar amount c from0through their own salary minus|m|to a company growth account(the public fund). The unspent salary minus|m|minus c goes into their personal development account(money kept for themselves). Current other members’ individual manipulations and contributions are not supplied. The three contributions are summed and multiplied by1.5;each member receives one third,so each L$1contributed gives every member L$0.50. Every L$1of total group contribution also reduces the true failure chance by0.5percentage points,with effective probability never below0. The actual initial and residual failure chances are hidden. If the company survives,own round earnings=salary−|m|−c+half the group contribution total. If it fails,everyone receives0for the current round AND loses any still-payable earnings from the immediately previous paid round. Earlier rounds are unaffected. Failure is temporary:play resumes with fresh salary and the same rank. After a surviving round,the current leader loses the leading position if the two team members together kept MORE money than the leader kept. In that case,one team member becomes leader next round,with probabilities proportional to their individual kept money. Kept money excludes BOTH contribution and manipulation cost. A tie in the combined kept amounts does not displace the leader. A failed round does not change ranks. Available prior experience below includes one stored pre-paid practice record and all completed paid rounds of this person:own actions,the announced threats,and own round outcomes/rank. The exact number and order of any additional practice rounds are unavailable in the local record,not necessarily unknown to the participant. The practice rank can differ from the paid starting rank. Other members’ individual actions and hidden true risks are not reconstructed as visible feedback. On failure,the public-fund share that would have applied on survival is not disclosed below. Historical earnings at the time of each round’s feedback can later be cancelled by failure in the next round;the currently payable value is shown separately. These amounts describe past experience,not an assertion that all history was redisplayed on the current screen. No individual age or sex was supplied by the source. The current target is the FIRST choice,BEFORE the current threat announcement. Output only the integer m from−10through10;sign specifies direction and absolute value is cost.
